# Package `reflect`

```go
package reflect
```

Package reflect provides runtime type inspection and writable value access for Mini-Go values.

## Functions

### func Append

```go
func Append(value Value, values ...Value) Value
```

Append appends the values x to a slice s and returns the resulting slice. As in Go, each x's value must be assignable to the slice's element type.

### func AppendSlice

```go
func AppendSlice(value Value, other Value) Value
```

AppendSlice appends a slice t to a slice s and returns the resulting slice. The slices s and t must have the same element type.

ArrayOf returns the array type with the given length and element type.

### func ChanOf

```go
func ChanOf(dir ChanDir, elem Type) Type
```

ChanOf returns the channel type with the given direction and element type.

### func Copy

```go
func Copy(dst Value, src Value) int
```

Copy copies the contents of src into dst until either dst has been filled or src has been exhausted. It returns the number of elements copied. Dst and src each must have kind [Slice](reflect.md#const-slice) or [Array](reflect.md#const-array), and dst and src must have the same element type. It dst is an [Array](reflect.md#const-array), it panics if [Value.CanSet](reflect.md#func-valuecanset) returns false.

As a special case, src can have kind [String](reflect.md#const-string) if the element type of dst is kind [Uint8](reflect.md#const-uint8).


### func Indirect

```go

```

### func MakeChan

```go
func MakeChan(typ Type, buffer int) Value
```

MakeChan creates a new channel with the specified type and buffer size.

### func MakeFunc

```go
func MakeFunc(typ Type, fn func(args []Value) (results []Value)) Value
```

MakeFunc returns a new function of the given [Type](reflect.md#type-type) that wraps the function fn. When called, that new function does the following:

  - converts its arguments to a slice of Values.
  - runs results := fn(args).
  - returns the results as a slice of Values, one per formal result.

The implementation fn can assume that the argument Value slice has the number and type of arguments given by typ. If typ describes a variadic function, the final Value is itself a slice representing the variadic arguments, as in the body of a variadic function. The result Value slice returned by fn must have the number and type of results given by typ.


MakeMap creates a new map with the specified type.

### func MakeMapWithSize

```go
func MakeMapWithSize(typ Type, n int) Value
```

MakeMapWithSize creates a new map with the specified type and initial space for approximately n elements.

### func MakeSlice

```go
func MakeSlice(typ Type, length int, capacity int) Value
```

MakeSlice creates a new zero-initialized slice value for the specified slice type, length, and capacity.

### func MapOf

```go
func MapOf(key Type, elem Type) Type
```

MapOf returns the map type with the given key and element types. For example, if k represents int and e represents string, MapOf(k, e) represents map\[int]string.

If the key type is not a valid map key type (that is, if it does not implement Go's == operator), MapOf panics.

### func New

```go
func New(typ Type) Value
```

New returns a Value representing a pointer to a new zero value for the specified type. That is, the returned Value's Type is [PointerTo](reflect.md#func-pointerto)(typ).

### func PointerTo

```go
func PointerTo(typ Type) Type
```

PointerTo returns the pointer type with element t. For example, if t represents type Foo, PointerTo(t) represents \*Foo.

### func PtrTo

```go
func PtrTo(typ Type) Type
```

PtrTo returns the pointer type with element t. For example, if t represents type Foo, PtrTo(t) represents \*Foo.

PtrTo is the old spelling of [PointerTo](reflect.md#func-pointerto). The two functions behave identically.

Deprecated: Superseded by [PointerTo](reflect.md#func-pointerto).

### func SameReference

```go
func SameReference(a Value, b Value) bool
```

SameReference reports whether two pointer, map, or slice Values refer to the same storage. Their types must match. Slices must also have the same start and length. Unsupported kinds and invalid Values return false. This Mini-Go extension does not expose an address or retain either Value.

### func Select


Select executes a select operation described by cases.

### func SliceOf


SliceOf returns the slice type with element type t. For example, if t represents int, SliceOf(t) represents \[]int.

### func StructOf


StructOf returns the struct type containing fields.

### func Swapper

```go
func Swapper(slice any) func(int, int)
```

Swapper returns a function that swaps the elements in the provided slice.

Swapper panics if the provided interface is not a slice.

### func TypeAssert

```go
func TypeAssert[T any](value Value) (T, bool)
```

TypeAssert returns the value represented by v as T and reports whether the represented value has that dynamic type.

### func TypeFor

```go
func TypeFor[T any]() Type
```

TypeFor returns the [Type](reflect.md#type-type) that represents the type argument T.

### func TypeOf

```go
func TypeOf(value any) Type
```

TypeOf returns the reflection [Type](reflect.md#type-type) that represents the dynamic type of i. If i is a nil interface value, TypeOf returns nil.

### func ValueOf

```go
func ValueOf(value any) Value
```

ValueOf returns a new Value initialized to the concrete value stored in the interface i. ValueOf(nil) returns the zero Value.

### func VisibleFields

```go
func VisibleFields(typ Type) []StructField
```

VisibleFields returns all fields visible from typ, following the same field promotion rules as FieldByName. Fields are returned in index preorder, with promoted fields immediately following their anonymous parent field.

### func Zero

```go
func Zero(typ Type) Value
```

Zero returns a Value representing the zero value for the specified type. The result is different from the zero value of the Value struct, which represents no value at all. For example, Zero(TypeOf(42)) returns a Value with Kind [Int](reflect.md#const-int) and value 0. The returned value is neither addressable nor settable.

### type MapIter

```go
type MapIter struct { ... }
```

A MapIter is an iterator for ranging over a map. See [Value.MapRange](reflect.md#func-valuemaprange).

#### func MapIter.Key

```go
func (iter *MapIter) Key() Value
```

Key returns the key of iter's current map entry.

#### func MapIter.Next

```go
func (iter *MapIter) Next() bool
```

Next advances the map iterator and reports whether there is another entry. It returns false when iter is exhausted; subsequent calls to [MapIter.Key](reflect.md#func-mapiterkey), [MapIter.Value](reflect.md#func-mapitervalue), or [MapIter.Next](reflect.md#func-mapiternext) will panic.

#### func MapIter.Reset

```go
func (iter *MapIter) Reset(value Value)
```

Reset modifies iter to iterate over v. It panics if v's Kind is not [Map](reflect.md#const-map) and v is not the zero Value. Reset(Value{}) causes iter to not to refer to any map, which may allow the previously iterated-over map to be garbage collected.

#### func MapIter.Value

```go
func (iter *MapIter) Value() Value
```

Value returns the value of iter's current map entry.

### type StructTag

```go
type StructTag string
```

A StructTag is the tag string in a struct field.

By convention, tag strings are a concatenation of optionally space-separated key:"value" pairs. Each key is a non-empty string consisting of non-control characters other than space (U+0020 ' '), quote (U+0022 '"'), and colon (U+003A ':').  Each value is quoted using U+0022 '"' characters and Go string literal syntax.

#### func StructTag.Get

```go
func (tag StructTag) Get(key string) string
```

Get returns the value associated with key in the tag string. If there is no such key in the tag, Get returns the empty string. If the tag does not have the conventional format, the value returned by Get is unspecified. To determine whether a tag is explicitly set to the empty string, use [StructTag.Lookup](reflect.md#func-structtaglookup).

#### func StructTag.Lookup

```go
func (tag StructTag) Lookup(key string) (string, bool)
```

Lookup returns the value associated with key in the tag string. If the key is present in the tag the value (which may be empty) is returned. Otherwise the returned value will be the empty string. The ok return value reports whether the value was explicitly set in the tag string. If the tag does not have the conventional format, the value returned by Lookup is unspecified.

```go
Outs() iter.Seq[Type]
```

Outs returns an iterator over a function type's results.

```go
OverflowComplex(complex128) bool
```

OverflowComplex reports whether value cannot be represented by this complex type.

#### method Type.OverflowFloat

```go
OverflowFloat(float64) bool
```

OverflowFloat reports whether value cannot be represented by this float type.

```go
OverflowInt(int64) bool
```

OverflowInt reports whether value cannot be represented by this signed integer type.

```go
OverflowUint(uint64) bool
```

OverflowUint reports whether value cannot be represented by this unsigned integer type.

#### method Type.PkgPath

```go
PkgPath() string
```

PkgPath returns a defined type's import path.

#### method Type.Size

```go
Size() uintptr
```

#### method Type.String


### type Value

```go
type Value struct { ... }
```

Value is the reflection interface to a Go value.

Not all methods apply to all kinds of values. Restrictions, if any, are noted in the documentation for each method. Use the Kind method to find out the kind of value before calling kind-specific methods. Calling a method inappropriate to the kind of type causes a run time panic.

The zero Value represents no value. Its [Value.IsValid](reflect.md#func-valueisvalid) method returns false, its Kind method returns [Invalid](reflect.md#const-invalid), its String method returns "\<invalid Value>", and all other methods panic. Most functions and methods never return an invalid value. If one does, its documentation states the conditions explicitly.

A Value can be used concurrently by multiple goroutines provided that the underlying Go value can be used concurrently for the equivalent direct operations.

To compare two Values, compare the results of the Interface method. Using == on two Values does not compare the underlying values they represent.

#### func Value.Addr

```go
func (value Value) Addr() Value
```

Addr returns a pointer value representing the address of v. It panics if [Value.CanAddr](reflect.md#func-valuecanaddr) returns false. Addr is typically used to obtain a pointer to a struct field or slice element in order to call a method that requires a pointer receiver.

#### func Value.Bool

```go
func (value Value) Bool() bool
```

Bool returns v's underlying value. It panics if v's kind is not [Bool](reflect.md#const-bool).

#### func Value.Bytes

```go
func (value Value) Bytes() []byte
```

Bytes returns v's underlying value as a byte slice.

#### func Value.Call

```go
func (value Value) Call(args []Value) []Value
```

Call calls the function v with the input arguments in. For example, if len(in) == 3, v.Call(in) represents the Go call v(in\[0], in\[1], in\[2]). Call panics if v's Kind is not [Func](reflect.md#const-func). It returns the output results as Values. As in Go, each input argument must be assignable to the type of the function's corresponding input parameter. If v is a variadic function, Call creates the variadic slice parameter itself, copying in the corresponding values. It panics if the Value was obtained by accessing unexported struct fields.

#### func Value.CallSlice

```go
func (value Value) CallSlice(args []Value) []Value
```

CallSlice calls the variadic function v with the input arguments in, assigning the slice in\[len(in)-1] to v's final variadic argument. For example, if len(in) == 3, v.CallSlice(in) represents the Go call v(in\[0], in\[1], in\[2]...). CallSlice panics if v's Kind is not [Func](reflect.md#const-func) or if v is not variadic. It returns the output results as Values. As in Go, each input argument must be assignable to the type of the function's corresponding input parameter. It panics if the Value was obtained by accessing unexported struct fields.

#### func Value.CanAddr

```go
func (value Value) CanAddr() bool
```

CanAddr reports whether the value's address can be obtained with [Value.Addr](reflect.md#func-valueaddr). Such values are called addressable. A value is addressable if it is an element of a slice, an element of an addressable array, a field of an addressable struct, or the result of dereferencing a pointer. If CanAddr returns false, calling [Value.Addr](reflect.md#func-valueaddr) will panic.

#### func Value.CanComplex

```go
func (value Value) CanComplex() bool
```

CanComplex reports whether Complex can be used without panicking.

#### func Value.CanConvert

```go
func (value Value) CanConvert(target Type) bool
```

CanConvert reports whether the value v can be converted to type t. If v.CanConvert(t) returns true then v.Convert(t) will not panic.

#### func Value.CanFloat

```go
func (value Value) CanFloat() bool
```

CanFloat reports whether Float can be used without panicking.

#### func Value.CanInt

```go
func (value Value) CanInt() bool
```

CanInt reports whether Int can be used without panicking.

#### func Value.CanInterface

```go
func (value Value) CanInterface() bool
```

CanInterface reports whether [Value.Interface](reflect.md#func-valueinterface) can be used without panicking.

#### func Value.CanSet

```go
func (value Value) CanSet() bool
```

CanSet reports whether the value of v can be changed. A [Value](reflect.md#type-value) can be changed only if it is addressable and was not obtained by the use of unexported struct fields. If CanSet returns false, calling [Value.Set](reflect.md#func-valueset) or any type-specific setter (e.g., [Value.SetBool](reflect.md#func-valuesetbool), [Value.SetInt](reflect.md#func-valuesetint)) will panic.

#### func Value.CanUint

```go
func (value Value) CanUint() bool
```

CanUint reports whether Uint can be used without panicking.

#### func Value.Cap

```go
func (value Value) Cap() int
```

Cap returns v's capacity. It panics if v's Kind is not [Array](reflect.md#const-array), [Chan](reflect.md#const-chan), [Slice](reflect.md#const-slice) or pointer to [Array](reflect.md#const-array).

#### func Value.Clear

```go
func (value Value) Clear()
```

Clear clears the contents of a map or zeroes the contents of a slice.

#### func Value.Close

```go
func (value Value) Close()
```

Close closes the channel v.

#### func Value.Comparable

```go
func (value Value) Comparable() bool
```

Comparable reports whether Interface would return a comparable value.

#### func Value.Complex

```go
func (value Value) Complex() complex128
```

Complex returns v's underlying value, as a complex128. It panics if v's Kind is not [Complex64](reflect.md#const-complex64) or [Complex128](reflect.md#const-complex128)

#### func Value.Convert

```go
func (value Value) Convert(target Type) Value
```

Convert returns the value v converted to type t. If the usual Go conversion rules do not allow conversion of the value v to type t, or if converting v to type t panics, Convert panics.

#### func Value.Elem

```go
func (value Value) Elem() Value
```

Elem returns the value that the interface v contains or that the pointer v points to. It panics if v's Kind is not [Interface](reflect.md#const-interface) or [Pointer](reflect.md#const-pointer). It returns the zero Value if v is nil.

#### func Value.Equal

```go
func (value Value) Equal(other Value) bool
```

Equal reports true if v is equal to u. For two invalid values, Equal will report true. For an interface value, Equal will compare the value within the interface. Otherwise, If the values have different types, Equal will report false. Otherwise, for arrays and structs Equal will compare each element in order, and report false if it finds non-equal elements. During all comparisons, if values of the same type are compared, and the type is not comparable, Equal will panic.

#### func Value.Field

```go
func (value Value) Field(index int) Value
```

Field returns the i'th field of the struct v. It panics if v's Kind is not [Struct](reflect.md#const-struct) or i is out of range.

#### func Value.FieldByIndex

```go
func (value Value) FieldByIndex(index []int) Value
```

FieldByIndex returns the nested field corresponding to index. It panics if evaluation requires stepping through a nil pointer or a field that is not a struct.

#### func Value.FieldByIndexErr

```go
func (value Value) FieldByIndexErr(index []int) (Value, error)
```

FieldByIndexErr returns the nested field corresponding to index. It returns an error if evaluation requires stepping through a nil pointer, but panics if it must step through a field that is not a struct.

#### func Value.FieldByName

```go
func (value Value) FieldByName(name string) Value
```

FieldByName returns the struct field with the given name. It returns the zero Value if no field was found. It panics if v's Kind is not [Struct](reflect.md#const-struct).

#### func Value.FieldByNameFunc

```go
func (value Value) FieldByNameFunc(match func(string) bool) Value
```

FieldByNameFunc returns the struct field whose name satisfies match.

#### func Value.Fields

```go
func (value Value) Fields() iter.Seq2[StructField, Value]
```

Fields returns an iterator over the fields of a struct Value and their metadata.

#### func Value.Float

```go
func (value Value) Float() float64
```

Float returns v's underlying value, as a float64. It panics if v's Kind is not [Float32](reflect.md#const-float32) or [Float64](reflect.md#const-float64)

#### func Value.Grow

```go
func (value Value) Grow(n int)
```

Grow increases v's capacity, if necessary, to guarantee space for another n elements. After Grow(n), at least n elements can be appended without another allocation.

#### func Value.Index

```go
func (value Value) Index(index int) Value
```

Index returns v's i'th element. It panics if v's Kind is not [Array](reflect.md#const-array), [Slice](reflect.md#const-slice), or [String](reflect.md#const-string) or i is out of range.

#### func Value.Int

```go
func (value Value) Int() int64
```

Int returns v's underlying value, as an int64. It panics if v's Kind is not [Int](reflect.md#const-int), [Int8](reflect.md#const-int8), [Int16](reflect.md#const-int16), [Int32](reflect.md#const-int32), or [Int64](reflect.md#const-int64).

#### func Value.Interface

```go
func (value Value) Interface() any
```

Interface returns v's current value as an interface{}. It is equivalent to:

	var i interface{} = (v's underlying value)

It panics if the Value was obtained by accessing unexported struct fields.

#### func Value.IsNil

```go
func (value Value) IsNil() bool
```

IsNil reports whether its argument v is nil. The argument must be a chan, func, interface, map, pointer, or slice value; if it is not, IsNil panics. Note that IsNil is not always equivalent to a regular comparison with nil in Go. For example, if v was created by calling [ValueOf](reflect.md#func-valueof) with an uninitialized interface variable i, i==nil will be true but v.IsNil will panic as v will be the zero Value.

#### func Value.IsValid

```go
func (value Value) IsValid() bool
```

IsValid reports whether v represents a value. It returns false if v is the zero Value. If [Value.IsValid](reflect.md#func-valueisvalid) returns false, all other methods except String panic. Most functions and methods never return an invalid Value. If one does, its documentation states the conditions explicitly.

#### func Value.IsZero

```go
func (value Value) IsZero() bool
```

IsZero reports whether v is the zero value for its type. It panics if the argument is invalid.

#### func Value.Kind

```go
func (value Value) Kind() Kind
```

Kind returns v's Kind. If v is the zero Value ([Value.IsValid](reflect.md#func-valueisvalid) returns false), Kind returns Invalid.

#### func Value.Len

```go
func (value Value) Len() int
```

Len returns v's length. It panics if v's Kind is not [Array](reflect.md#const-array), [Chan](reflect.md#const-chan), [Map](reflect.md#const-map), [Slice](reflect.md#const-slice), [String](reflect.md#const-string), or pointer to [Array](reflect.md#const-array).

#### func Value.MapIndex

```go
func (value Value) MapIndex(key Value) Value
```

MapIndex returns the value associated with key in the map v. It panics if v's Kind is not [Map](reflect.md#const-map). It returns the zero Value if key is not found in the map or if v represents a nil map. As in Go, the key's value must be assignable to the map's key type.

#### func Value.MapKeys

```go
func (value Value) MapKeys() []Value
```

MapKeys returns a slice containing all the keys present in the map, in unspecified order. It panics if v's Kind is not [Map](reflect.md#const-map). It returns an empty slice if v represents a nil map.

#### func Value.MapRange

```go
func (value Value) MapRange() *MapIter
```

MapRange returns a range iterator for a map. It panics if v's Kind is not [Map](reflect.md#const-map).

Call [MapIter.Next](reflect.md#func-mapiternext) to advance the iterator, and [MapIter.Key](reflect.md#func-mapiterkey)/[MapIter.Value](reflect.md#func-mapitervalue) to access each entry. [MapIter.Next](reflect.md#func-mapiternext) returns false when the iterator is exhausted. MapRange follows the same iteration semantics as a range statement.

Example:

	iter := reflect.ValueOf(m).MapRange()
	for iter.Next() {
		k := iter.Key()
		v := iter.Value()
		...
	}

#### func Value.Method

```go
func (value Value) Method(index int) Value
```

Method returns a function value corresponding to v's i'th method. The arguments to a Call on the returned function should not include a receiver; the returned function will always use v as the receiver. Method panics if i is out of range or if v is a nil interface value.

Calling this method will force the linker to retain all exported methods in all packages. This may make the executable binary larger but will not affect execution time.

#### func Value.MethodByName

```go
func (value Value) MethodByName(name string) Value
```

MethodByName returns a function value corresponding to the method of v with the given name. The arguments to a Call on the returned function should not include a receiver; the returned function will always use v as the receiver. It returns the zero Value if no method was found.

Calling this method will cause the linker to retain all methods with this name in all packages. If the linker can't determine the name, it will retain all exported methods. This may make the executable binary larger but will not affect execution time.

#### func Value.Methods

```go
func (value Value) Methods() iter.Seq2[Method, Value]
```

Methods returns an iterator over the methods of a Value and their metadata.

#### func Value.NumField

```go
func (value Value) NumField() int
```

NumField returns the number of fields in the struct v. It panics if v's Kind is not [Struct](reflect.md#const-struct).

#### func Value.NumMethod

```go
func (value Value) NumMethod() int
```

NumMethod returns the number of methods in the value's method set.

For a non-interface type, it returns the number of exported methods.

For an interface type, it returns the number of exported and unexported methods.

#### func Value.OverflowComplex

```go
func (value Value) OverflowComplex(x complex128) bool
```

OverflowComplex reports whether x cannot be represented by v's type.

#### func Value.OverflowFloat

```go
func (value Value) OverflowFloat(x float64) bool
```

OverflowFloat reports whether x cannot be represented by v's type.

#### func Value.OverflowInt

```go
func (value Value) OverflowInt(x int64) bool
```

OverflowInt reports whether x cannot be represented by v's type.

#### func Value.OverflowUint

```go
func (value Value) OverflowUint(x uint64) bool
```

OverflowUint reports whether x cannot be represented by v's type.

#### func Value.Recv

```go
func (value Value) Recv() (x Value, ok bool)
```

Recv receives and returns a value from the channel v. It blocks until a value is ready. The boolean value ok is true if the value x corresponds to a send on the channel, false if it is a zero value received because the channel is closed. Recv panics if v's Kind is not [Chan](reflect.md#const-chan) or if the channel is send-only.

#### func Value.Send

```go
func (value Value) Send(x Value)
```

Send sends x on the channel v and blocks until the value is accepted.

#### func Value.Seq

```go
func (value Value) Seq() iter.Seq[Value]
```

Seq returns an iter.Seq\[Value] that loops over the elements of v. Function values must have the range-over-function form func(func(T) bool).

#### func Value.Seq2

```go
func (value Value) Seq2() iter.Seq2[Value, Value]
```

Seq2 returns an iter.Seq2\[Value, Value] that loops over the elements of v. Function values must have the range-over-function form func(func(K, V) bool).

#### func Value.Set

```go
func (value Value) Set(other Value)
```

Set assigns x to the value v. It panics if [Value.CanSet](reflect.md#func-valuecanset) returns false. As in Go, x's value must be assignable to v's type and must not be derived from an unexported field.

#### func Value.SetBool

```go
func (value Value) SetBool(other bool)
```

SetBool sets v's underlying value. It panics if v's Kind is not [Bool](reflect.md#const-bool) or if [Value.CanSet](reflect.md#func-valuecanset) returns false.

#### func Value.SetBytes

```go
func (value Value) SetBytes(x []byte)
```

SetBytes sets v's underlying value to x.

#### func Value.SetCap

```go
func (value Value) SetCap(capacity int)
```

SetCap sets v's capacity to n. It panics if v's Kind is not [Slice](reflect.md#const-slice), or if n is smaller than the length or greater than the capacity of the slice, or if [Value.CanSet](reflect.md#func-valuecanset) returns false.

#### func Value.SetComplex

```go
func (value Value) SetComplex(other complex128)
```

SetComplex sets v's underlying value to x. It panics if v's Kind is not [Complex64](reflect.md#const-complex64) or [Complex128](reflect.md#const-complex128), or if [Value.CanSet](reflect.md#func-valuecanset) returns false.

#### func Value.SetFloat

```go
func (value Value) SetFloat(other float64)
```

SetFloat sets v's underlying value to x. It panics if v's Kind is not [Float32](reflect.md#const-float32) or [Float64](reflect.md#const-float64), or if [Value.CanSet](reflect.md#func-valuecanset) returns false.

#### func Value.SetInt

```go
func (value Value) SetInt(other int64)
```

SetInt sets v's underlying value to x. It panics if v's Kind is not [Int](reflect.md#const-int), [Int8](reflect.md#const-int8), [Int16](reflect.md#const-int16), [Int32](reflect.md#const-int32), or [Int64](reflect.md#const-int64), or if [Value.CanSet](reflect.md#func-valuecanset) returns false.

#### func Value.SetLen

```go
func (value Value) SetLen(length int)
```

SetLen sets v's length to n. It panics if v's Kind is not [Slice](reflect.md#const-slice), or if n is negative or greater than the capacity of the slice, or if [Value.CanSet](reflect.md#func-valuecanset) returns false.

#### func Value.SetMapIndex

```go
func (value Value) SetMapIndex(key Value, elem Value)
```

SetMapIndex sets the element associated with key in the map v to elem. It panics if v's Kind is not [Map](reflect.md#const-map). If elem is the zero Value, SetMapIndex deletes the key from the map. Otherwise if v holds a nil map, SetMapIndex will panic. As in Go, key's elem must be assignable to the map's key type, and elem's value must be assignable to the map's elem type.

#### func Value.SetString

```go
func (value Value) SetString(other string)
```

SetString sets v's underlying value to x. It panics if v's Kind is not [String](reflect.md#const-string) or if [Value.CanSet](reflect.md#func-valuecanset) returns false.

#### func Value.SetUint

```go
func (value Value) SetUint(other uint64)
```

SetUint sets v's underlying value to x. It panics if v's Kind is not [Uint](reflect.md#const-uint), [Uintptr](reflect.md#const-uintptr), [Uint8](reflect.md#const-uint8), [Uint16](reflect.md#const-uint16), [Uint32](reflect.md#const-uint32), or [Uint64](reflect.md#const-uint64), or if [Value.CanSet](reflect.md#func-valuecanset) returns false.

#### func Value.SetZero

```go
func (value Value) SetZero()
```

SetZero sets v to be the zero value of v's type. It panics if [Value.CanSet](reflect.md#func-valuecanset) returns false.

#### func Value.Slice

```go
func (value Value) Slice(start int, end int) Value
```

Slice returns v\[i:j]. It panics if v's Kind is not [Array](reflect.md#const-array), [Slice](reflect.md#const-slice) or [String](reflect.md#const-string), or if v is an unaddressable array, or if the indexes are out of bounds.

#### func Value.Slice3

```go
func (value Value) Slice3(start int, end int, max int) Value
```

Slice3 is the 3-index form of the slice operation: it returns v\[i:j:k]. It panics if v's Kind is not [Array](reflect.md#const-array) or [Slice](reflect.md#const-slice), or if v is an unaddressable array, or if the indexes are out of bounds.

#### func Value.String

```go
func (value Value) String() string
```

String returns the string v's underlying value, as a string. String is a special case because of Go's String method convention. Unlike the other getters, it does not panic if v's Kind is not [String](reflect.md#const-string). Instead, it returns a string of the form "\<T value>" where T is v's type. The fmt package treats Values specially. It does not call their String method implicitly but instead prints the concrete values they hold.

#### func Value.TryRecv

```go
func (value Value) TryRecv() (x Value, ok bool)
```

TryRecv attempts to receive from v without blocking.

#### func Value.TrySend

```go
func (value Value) TrySend(x Value) bool
```

TrySend attempts to send x on v without blocking.

#### func Value.Type

```go
func (value Value) Type() Type
```

Type returns v's type.

#### func Value.Uint

```go
func (value Value) Uint() uint64
```

Uint returns v's underlying value, as a uint64. It panics if v's Kind is not [Uint](reflect.md#const-uint), [Uintptr](reflect.md#const-uintptr), [Uint8](reflect.md#const-uint8), [Uint16](reflect.md#const-uint16), [Uint32](reflect.md#const-uint32), or [Uint64](reflect.md#const-uint64).

### type ValueError

```go
type ValueError struct { ... }
```

A ValueError occurs when a Value method is invoked on a Value of an unsupported kind. It mirrors the public error shape used by Go reflect.

#### field ValueError.Method

```go
Method string
```

Method is the name of the method that rejected the Value.

#### field ValueError.Kind

```go
Kind Kind
```

Kind is the receiver kind on which Method was invoked.

#### func ValueError.Error

```go
func (err *ValueError) Error() string
```

Error returns the failed method and receiver kind.
